name: U.S. Office of Personnel Management

summary.text: The U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is the federal government's central human-resources agency. On February 6, 2026 it published a final rule (91 Fed. Reg. 5580) implementing Schedule Policy/Career, a new excepted-service category created by Executive Order 14171 of January 20, 2025 and formerly known as Schedule F; OPM projected about 50,000 positions would be moved into it, with agencies recommending positions and the President designating them by executive order. OPM and the Office of Management and Budget also issued the February 2025 memorandum implementing Executive Order 14210 on agency reductions in force, which the Supreme Court allowed to proceed on July 8, 2025 by staying a district-court injunction in Trump v. AFGE.

facts.claim: OPM's final rule 'Improving Performance, Accountability, and Responsiveness in the Civil Service' (91 Fed. Reg. 5580, February 6, 2026) implements Schedule Policy/Career, a new excepted-service category created by Executive Order 14171 of January 20, 2025. The rule took effect in March 2026 (sources give March 8 or March 9).
facts.quote: The rule is Improving Performance, Accountability, and Responsiveness in the Civil Service (91 Fed. Reg. 5580; Feb. 6, 2026).

sources.title: Schedule Policy/Career: 2026 Final Rule, Legal Challenges, and Issues for Lawmakers

facts.claim: The final rule projects that approximately 50,000 positions would be moved into Schedule Policy/Career. The rule does not itself place positions: agencies recommend positions to OPM, OPM reviews the recommendations and sends them to the President, who must formally designate the positions by executive order. The rule applies to positions, not individuals.
facts.quote: Agencies will recommend positions for reclassification to OPM. OPM will then review those recommendations and send them to President Donald Trump, who must formally designate the positions by executive order.

facts.claim: Lawsuits challenging Schedule Policy/Career are pending: on March 17, 2026 a court accepted the National Treasury Employees Union's proposal to file an amended complaint within 14 days of a presidential executive order placing positions in the schedule, and Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility and four unions filed a separate challenge in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland.
facts.quote: on March 17, 2026, the court accepted the NTEU's proposal to file an amended complaint within 14 days of the President issuing an executive order that places positions in Schedule Policy/Career

facts.claim: On May 22, 2025 Judge Susan Illston of the Northern District of California issued a preliminary injunction blocking large-scale layoffs and agency reorganizations ordered under Executive Order 14210 (signed February 11, 2025, implementing the 'Department of Government Efficiency Workforce Optimization Initiative') and the joint OMB-OPM memorandum implementing it, in a case brought by the American Federation of Government Employees and other unions.
facts.quote: Judge Susan Illston of the Northern District of California issued the preliminary injunction on May 22, 2025.

sources.title: Federal Court Halts Mass Layoffs in the Civil Service

sources.publisher: Supreme Court of the United States (docket)
sources.title: Trump v. AFGE, No. 24A1174, Application for Stay

facts.claim: On July 8, 2025 the Supreme Court stayed that injunction in Trump v. AFGE, finding the government likely to succeed on its argument that Executive Order 14210 and the OMB-OPM memorandum are lawful, while expressing no view on the legality of any specific agency RIF and reorganization plan. Reporting describes the vote as 8-1 with Justice Jackson dissenting and Justice Sotomayor concurring.
facts.quote: Because the Government is likely to succeed on its argument that the Executive Order and Memorandum are lawful—and because the other factors bearing on whether to grant a stay are satisfied—we grant the application.

connections.claim: AFGE and other unions sued over Executive Order 14210 and the OMB-OPM implementing memorandum; a district court enjoined the layoffs on May 22, 2025, and the Supreme Court stayed that injunction on July 8, 2025.
connections.quote: We express no view on the legality of any Agency RIF and Reorganization Plan produced or approved pursuant to the Executive Order and Memorandum.

openQuestions: How many positions have actually been designated into Schedule Policy/Career by executive order (OPM's page lists a June 8, 2026 memorandum on Executive Order 14410) was not determined.
The page attributes the strategy to Curtis Yarvin's 'RAGE' framework; no official source links the rule to Yarvin (see curtis-yarvin.json for his own statements and JD Vance's 2021 remarks).
The Supreme Court order text was read from a copy posted by NRDC; confirm against the supremecourt.gov docket for No. 24A1174.
